note: Required acceptance blueprint. Pending is not a passing or skipped test. The final verifier must require actual runtime results for every ID.

cases.requirement: Different workspaces/installations cannot list, resolve, search, relate, mutate or deliver each other's data, even with equal local IDs/names.
Generic create/patch/import rejects undeclared fields, invalid enum/type/required/relationship values consistently across UI/API/tool/workflow; unique/CAS races produce one valid outcome.
CRM remains the same `entities` IDs/graph references; native module and generic records reference that canonical company with current access.
The native operations workflow enforces cost-field/role rules and approval state; its multi-record command/audit/outbox commits once or fully rolls back, including replay.
Two native frontends use one Brian backend. The portal user signs in through Brian, has no workspace membership and sees only granted records/fields.
App-data service/bot credentials are hashed, scoped, revocable and parent-bound; spoofed user/email/roles do not impersonate; existing chat/Brain/Home/OAuth audiences never cross.
Record/field denial covers query predicates, ordering, count/aggregate, relation pickers, graph/vector candidates, provenance, exports and direct IDs before exposure.
App/client/grant/field downgrade invalidates tokens' effective rights and running streams, confirmations, background/resumed work and client/offline caches.
A foreign department cannot discover/call a labelled connector or obtain its output via shared assistant, channel, cache, memory, consult, artifact or delivery.
Source verifies exact authenticated initiator and executing assistant plus issuer/workspace/instance/audience; unknown source mapping denies despite valid Brian authentication.
Forged, expired, wrong-alg/type/key, body-swapped, user/assistant-swapped, cross-instance/tenant and replayed actor assertions fail. Fresh retry preserves idempotency; rotation/revoke behaves as §6.
Same-department users retain different source record/field rights across direct and retained results; one user's revocation does not revoke another's independent grant.

Source withdrawal, stale/unverifiable access, outage or grant contraction blocks retrieval/replay/model context, derived writes and final delivery; missing external source never falls back to native historical `gone` semantics.
Actual light/REM/deep consolidation, compaction, KB/files, graph/CRM facts, tasks/Goals, workflow state and Page/Office artifacts preserve ancestor/field evidence without laundering.
Group recipients without applicable local/source rights receive no restricted tokens/files; a private authorized requester does not confer rights on the room.
Unattended and delegated work retains its named actor/parent grant; revocation between source read, approval, resume and effect/delivery stops further work; uncertain completed effects reconcile.

Governed retention checks current source access; independent snapshots need explicit release; ephemeral content leaves no protected transcript/tool/answer/cache/index bytes and is refused on an incompatible lane.
Legacy incomplete evidence remains held until the authorized product review/repair path qualifies it. Activation cannot bypass unresolved in-scope coverage or invent rights.
New modules and a second independent source fixture use published SDK profiles without editing another module's internals, core ACL rules or per-channel allowlists.
Fresh OSS/hosted-overlay migrations and representative legacy upgrade preserve IDs, existing grants, schema values, queued work and client compatibility; no applied migration changes.
UI/Brian management paths invoke identical services; secrets stay out of model/logs; four locales, 360px/desktop controls, live invalidation and safe retry states work.
The checked §8 ledger lists every in-scope consumer and its enforcing test; both editions consume the open implementation. Required tests/builds pass with no new baseline entries.
